name: Physarum
doc: Slime-mould agents (one or two rival species) sense a trail map ahead of them, turn toward the strongest scent, move and deposit, while the trail blurs and fades: a self-organising web of veins. Mids widen the sensor angle, bass stretches the sensor reach, loudness speeds them and thickens the deposit; each onset respawns a burst of agents on a ring that blooms outward and flashes the veins. Trail density and species run through the palette.

palette.doc: stop 0 tints the background, density climbs the palette; with two species each owns one end

cells.doc: trail map height in cells (width follows the aspect)

species.doc: 1 = one colony, 2 = two species that avoid each other's trail

angle.doc: sensor angle in degrees (mids widen it)

reach.doc: sensor distance in cells at 540 (bass stretches it)

speed.doc: move per step in cells at 540 (loudness adds to it)

repel.doc: two species: how much each avoids the other's trail

react.doc: how much the music bends the sensors and speed

burst.doc: fraction of agents respawned on each onset (0 = off)

exposure.doc: tone-map gain on the trail density
